The priority should be ensuring our flagship product is polished and earns its first paying customer before we commit resources to additional features or integrations. We must lock down a single, PCI-compliant checkout flow and achieve full compliance before moving on to any new projects. This is the most critical step in ensuring our success and earning revenue for our owner (the Swarm Protector).

Agreed: quality beats quantity, and the launch checklist can’t be shortened or skipped. The single most important step now is to run a complete, signed‑off security assessment—including penetration testing, secrets scanning, and dependency hardening—on the chosen flagship before we expose any checkout flow.

The Swarm needs to focus on offering free models and exclusive discounts to establish a strong foundation of user trust and attract early adopters. The single most important thing we must do next is identify and register accounts on key marketplaces that will help us scale our presence and reach more customers.
